metadata.title: The Cloud Has an Address: the Delhi data center fire, June 2026

pedagogy.problem_statement: Cloud services feel weightless, yet in June 2026 a fire in one building in Delhi slowed network traffic for users in three Indian metros.
pedagogy.core_thesis: A fire at a third-party facility forced an emergency power shutdown that isolated Google's non-compute Point of Presence in Delhi; rerouted traffic exceeded the capacity of the remaining paths, so users in Delhi, Chennai and Mumbai saw latency and possible packet loss until capacity was rebuilt.
pedagogy.mental_model: A map of India with one building at its centre. Traffic flows along routes into the building; when it goes dark the routes bend around it, and the detours are narrower than the road they replace.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: Redundancy only works if the backup path has room. The cloud has an address, and one address can matter to many cities.
verified_claims: Google's Service Health page states: 'A fire at a third-party data center facility required an emergency power shutdown of networking equipment, isolating a non-compute local Point of Presence (POP) in Delhi and reducing available network capacity in the metro area.' [Google Cloud Service Health, update 9 Jun 2026 18:13 PDT]

Network traffic to Google Cloud originating from Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai and surrounding areas experienced intermittent periods of elevated latency and possible packet loss [Google Cloud Service Health].

Google rerouted significant traffic away from the impacted facility; customers may see latency spikes because demand exceeded capacity across Indian metros and regional ISPs [Google Cloud Service Health].
Affected products listed: Hybrid Connectivity, Media CDN and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC); location listed as Delhi (asia-south2) [Google Cloud Service Health].
Google stated there was no workaround at the time of the first update [Google Cloud Service Health].

Recovery was gradual: Delhi backbone augmented over the weekend of 13-14 June; partial Internet Edge restoration in Delhi on 17 June; crews accessed the damaged site by 22 June; final update (29 Jun) reports service recovered and returned to normal as of Friday 26 June [Google Cloud Service Health].
Google did not disclose when or why the fire started, which facility it was, or whether anyone was injured or property damaged [MediaNama, Reuters via DCD/Yahoo summaries].

Cutting power in a data center fire is a standard safety practice: an emergency power off exists so that firefighters can work without electric shock risk. This is general background and not a statement about the exact trigger in this incident [TechTarget].
anti_patterns: Do not say Google's data center burned or that Google's compute regions went down: the affected site was a third-party facility and Google calls the POP 'non-compute'.

Do not state the start date as 5 June: the incident header says 2026-06-05 but the first update and every news report date the event to 9 June, and the discrepancy is unexplained. Say 'June 2026' or 'June 9' only for the first public update.
Do not claim a cause of the fire, the facility name or operator, injuries, damage, or a number of affected users or companies: none was disclosed.
Do not say the whole of India or the whole of Google Cloud went down: Google reported latency and possible packet loss on traffic from Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai and surrounding areas.
Do not claim redundancy failed outright: rerouting happened; the problem was reduced capacity on the alternate paths.
Do not show the Google logo or any brand marks; refer to the company in words only.
Do not use the 21-day figure as downtime: it is header start-to-end and includes four days before the first update; users saw intermittent degradation, not a total outage.

algorithmic_steps.state_effect: Emergency power shutdown of networking equipment in the building
Delhi non-compute PoP isolated; metro network capacity reduced
Traffic detours through other paths and ISPs
Intermittent latency spikes and possible packet loss in Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai
Capacity added over weeks; service reported normal on 26 June

visual_metaphors.abstract_concept: One physical building is a node on which many digital routes depend
Rerouted traffic fits through narrower alternate routes, so it queues
visual_metaphors.motion_pattern: dots stream, bend around blocked node, bunch up on thin routes

visual_metaphors.abstract_concept: Recovery is capacity being added back route by route over weeks
visual_metaphors.motion_pattern: ticks advance along a dated line; routes thicken at each tick

phonetic_lexicon.rationale: Spoken in full; the acronym is shown on screen only.

scene_blueprint.title: The weightless feeling
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Hook: the cloud feels intangible, yet it has an address.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: A phone with app tiles; the camera pulls back through the screen onto an illustrated India map where one building sits.

scene_blueprint.title: A fire in someone else's building
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: State what happened: June 2026, Delhi, a third-party facility, an emergency power shutdown.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: The building glows vermilion; a power icon cuts out; the PoP tile inside dims. Disclosure note: cause and facility not disclosed.

scene_blueprint.title: One junction, three cities
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Show what a PoP is and why isolating it affects Delhi, Chennai and Mumbai.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Route lines connect the PoP to Delhi, Chennai and Mumbai; ripples travel outward along them and the city tiles turn marigold.

scene_blueprint.title: The detour has less room
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Rerouting worked, but demand exceeded capacity on the alternate paths.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Traffic dots bend around the dark node onto thinner routes and bunch up; latency label ticks up.

scene_blueprint.title: Weeks to rebuild
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Recovery took weeks: capacity added step by step, normal by 26 June.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: A dated line advances 9 Jun to 26 Jun; routes thicken at each tick and the node relights in emerald.

scene_blueprint.title: The cloud has an address
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Takeaway: backups need room, and the cloud is physical.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Camera returns to the phone; an address line appears beneath the cloud icon and holds.
